title: MLKV shared cache + per-layer Mirror KV views
hypothesis: For layer K/V functions related by small role/layer coordinate changes, one shared physical K/V projection/cache plus layer-specific Givens codes recovers per-layer attention outputs while using less actual cache and model payload than multi-group MLKV, beating a same-byte gate.
physical_object: one shared K projection and one shared V projection/cache pair
mirror_coordinate: one Givens angle for each of four layers and two roles (K/V)
logical_multiplicity: four distinct logical layer K/V views from one cached pair
teacher: one shared K/V base, independently rotated per layer/role

development.selection_metric: mean development MSE across all five methods

cache.policy: materialize one K/V pair per MLKV group; Mirror derives each layer view from the shared cached base tensors
cache.measurement: sum numel × element_size for materialized cache tensors

storage.serialization: torch.save state_dict plus deterministic config JSON

success_gate: Each fresh world: Mirror MSE <=1.10x independent-layer MHA; at least10x lower than one-group hard MLKV; at least10% lower than scalar gate; model payload and actual materialized cache both at least25% below two-group MLKV.
failure_gate: Mirror misses any quality gate or same-byte gate control is within10% MSE.
boundaries: teacher exactly aligned to shared-base layer views
same memory input supplied to every layer; evolving hidden-state effects omitted
no natural text or autoregressive throughput claim
cache bytes are actual tensor payload, not allocator overhead
